name: Christian Socialism
summary: Christian socialism holds that the Gospel's concern for the poor, its condemnation of greed and its picture of shared goods in Acts call for a more cooperative economic order in place of competitive capitalism. It seeks social ownership, cooperatives, strong unions and a welfare state, pursued mainly by democratic persuasion and reform rather than class war. Its adherents range from pacifist and anarchist Christians to Labour-affiliated reformers and liberation theologians, and they are divided on moral and social questions such as abortion and same-sex marriage.
scope: The mainstream reforming strand: the British Christian Socialists (Maurice, Kingsley, Ludlow), the American Social Gospel (Rauschenbusch, Gladden), R. H. Tawney and the Labour-affiliated Christian Socialist Movement (now Christians on the Left). Marxist-influenced liberation theology, Christian anarchism and Catholic distributism are noted as variants but not the basis. Many answers on modern issues are inferred with low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Frederick Denison Maurice
keyFigures.role: Coined the term Christian socialism in 1848 and co-founded the British movement.

keyFigures.name: Walter Rauschenbusch
keyFigures.role: Baptist pastor and leading theologian of the Social Gospel.

keyFigures.name: R. H. Tawney
keyFigures.role: Economic historian and Christian socialist critic of the acquisitive society.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Christian socialists draw on Matthew 25 and care for the sick and poor, and the Labour-affiliated movement backs welfare-state provision; healthcare free at need follows from priority to the poor.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Social Gospel and British Christian socialists campaigned against sweated labour and long hours, so a wage floor fits, though wage law is not a defining text.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents see capitalism as rooted in greed (Tawney's acquisitive society), but cooperative and mixed-market forms are accepted, so disagreement rather than strong disagreement.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialism implies social ownership and Rauschenbusch opposed neither public property nor social ownership; strands favour cooperatives or mutuals over state control, so mild agreement.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Condemnation of hoarding (Basil, Chrysostom, James 5) and of property as power makes redistribution through higher taxes on the rich standard.

unions-good.rationale: Support for unions and cooperatives was core to Maurice and Ludlow and to Rauschenbusch and Gladden; Catholic teaching also treats the right to unionise as basic.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rauschenbusch calls property a stimulus to character but also an outlet for selfishness and a trust held for others, so it may be overridden for the common good.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposition to predatory profit and to concentrated control of land and tools leads to firm regulation of corporations, as in Social Gospel reform campaigns.

cut-welfare.rationale: Care for the destitute is a central Christian-socialist duty (Ruskin, Matthew 25); cutting welfare reverses it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Producer cooperatives were the original Christian-socialist project (Ludlow, Maurice) and Rauschenbusch backed cooperatives, though not all adherents demand it generally.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on human dignity and that many Christian socialists are pacifist or anarchist, leaning against state surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between moralist reformers (Social Gospel prohibitionists) and compassion-based decriminalisers.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; concern for human dignity pulls toward restriction while free-expression traditions pull against, with no common line.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from belief in the worth of the common man as support for democratic institutions and from Christian anarchist strands; personal strongman rule is alien.

state-harmful.rationale: Mainstream Christian socialists want the state to secure justice and welfare; only the minority Christian-anarchist strand rejects the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the strong pacifist and anti-violence strands and the peace emphasis of Sermon on the Mount.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from pacifist tendencies and war as waste of life; adherents favour social over coercive solutions to order.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from view that sex work is exploitation of the poor, with liberal Christian socialists dissenting.

decide-locally.rationale: Cooperative and communal traditions favour local self-organisation, but national welfare and labour law pull the other way; no settled position.

rehabilitation.rationale: Christian ethics of forgiveness and human worth lead adherents to favour rehabilitation over retribution; inferred rather than quoted.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents split: Catholic and many Protestant strands stress family, while progressive strands do not; Rauschenbusch calls family the best case of solidarity.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Christian socialists split along church lines: Christians on the Left-type progressives accept it, Catholic and conservative strands do not.

abortion-legal.rationale: Left-leaning Christians prioritise poor and migrants but remain divided on abortion; the strand has no unified position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents want Christian ethics to shape politics (Christianizing the social order) but few want state-imposed religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Black Social Gospel and the later civil-rights tradition (King) applied Christian justice to race, and concern for the oppressed implies remedy.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; strands differ by theology and confession.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a concern of the tradition; internationalist ethics offset local and patriotic attachments.

gradual-change.rationale: Mainstream movements pursued socialism through persuasion, elections and reform, though prophetic critique of institutions is strong.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Concern for migrants and the stranger (a biblical theme) leads adherents to oppose cutting immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from universal brotherhood and peace emphasis; internationalism is common but not a stated tenet.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from critique of competition and acquisitiveness; many favour fair-trade rather than unregulated trade.

nation-first.rationale: Universal fellowship and war as rupture of fellowship make putting national interest above cooperation contrary to the creed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Pacifist strands oppose war while others accept it to protect the weak; adherents are split.

open-borders.rationale: Hospitality to the stranger pulls toward open borders, but few adherents demand them; inferred and split.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; stewardship and anti-acquisitiveness pull toward limits, social-welfare aims toward growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a historic issue; modern Christian socialists treat creation care and justice for the poor as reasons for strong action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Anti-acquisitive moralism suggests problems are moral rather than technical; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed and split between peace and climate concerns.

revolution-justified.rationale: Source notes Christian socialists were committed to democratic methods and persuasion; liberation-theology strands are an exception.

experts-over-public.rationale: Belief in the worth and capacity of the common man as spiritual basis of democracy cuts against technocracy; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Strands vary from guild and cooperative socialism to state socialism; no common position.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperative ownership within market exchange was the original project and Rauschenbusch backed cooperatives, so markets under worker or public ownership are acceptable.

land-value-tax.rationale: Henry George's Progress and Poverty inspired the Social Gospel, and Ruskin and Rauschenbusch criticised unearned land income, but a single tax is not a Christian-socialist tenet.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rauschenbusch objects to income without productive labour, which supports taxing inherited wealth; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; support for strong welfare is clear but unconditional payment is not a doctrine.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed and no clear Christian-socialist line.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Strands range from cooperative to state-led socialism; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rauschenbusch wants to conserve and spread the blessings of property and views cooperation as the route for small producers; distributist cousins press this harder.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rauschenbusch questions the wages system but no mainstream adherent demands abolishing money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; economic critique is of greed, not central banking, though some distributists distrust finance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Catholic social teaching and Anglican strands favour guild and corporate bodies, while others favour free unions; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Commitment to democratic methods and the worth of the common man make single-party rule contrary to the tradition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition leans democratic and egalitarian, though Anglican adherents have lived under constitutional monarchies.

democracy-best.rationale: Source says Christian socialists were committed to democratic methods and Rauschenbusch ties democracy to human worth.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; democratic but no stance on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Cooperative and guild forms resemble councils but Christian socialists work through parliaments, so split.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources record no Christian-socialist position on secession; Plaid Cymru's Christian socialists back self-government but the wider tradition is silent, so neutral.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal worth of persons and the claim that Jesus took the side of common people contradict natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Christian anarchist and pacifist strands say never, while liberation theology accepts revolution; adherents are genuinely split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Rauschenbusch calls war a wholesale waster of life and a rupture of fellowship.

separate-church-state.rationale: Strands range from established-church Anglicans to strict separationists; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ethical inspiration from the Bible is central but adherents seek persuasion in democracies, not scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Opposition to market solutions for public goods and favour for state guaranteeing justice; even anarchists reject profit-based defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Universal brotherhood and equal worth of all people contradict ethnic nation-building.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mainstream Christian socialists reject Marxist class struggle in favour of cooperation, though liberation theologians embrace it.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Tawney's Equality (1931) argued for an egalitarian society based on the infinite importance of every person, though adherents stress dignity over strict equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the concern for oppressed peoples and Social Gospel justice; not stated in sources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents are split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Universalism favours inclusiveness over religious blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Core critique of greed and the acquisitive society directly rejects self-interest as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Strong sense of duty to neighbour but equal dignity also grounds rights; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Creation care is common in modern Christian thinking, but not a historic tenet.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred; Catholic strands reject it and others see poverty as a distribution problem.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The tradition criticises capitalist industry but aims to reform it, not condemn civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on social institutions over speed of change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from theological conception of human dignity; not discussed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Belief in the capacity of ordinary people and moral responsibility suggests rejecting algorithmic rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Never addressed by the tradition, and its themes of dignity and distrust of state power pull in opposite directions, so neutral and low confidence.

restore-past-order.rationale: Prophetic orientation toward a better order to come, though some Anglo-Catholic strands admire medieval guilds.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Rooted in a moral vision of the Kingdom of God and principles, though reformers are pragmatic about means.

direct-action.rationale: Some Christian anarchists and liberation strands favour direct action but most work through elections and parliaments; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Christian pacifist and anarchist traditions insist on means reflecting ends, and the mainstream works by persuasion and election.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; clearly contrary to reform of industrial society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not an aim of any strand.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Acts 4 model of sharing goods as each has need is cited as Christian communism and an early-church ideal.

production-for-use.rationale: Rauschenbusch contrasts solidaristic feeling with predatory profit and approves property for use, not power.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rauschenbusch criticises predatory profit but not all profit; Marxist exploitation theory is rejected by the mainstream and accepted by others.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Democratic and Christian ethics reject dictatorial class power.

collective-farming.rationale: Cooperation for small farms is favoured but compulsory collectivisation is not.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rauschenbusch sees war as rupture of fellowship but causal claim is not a Christian-socialist tenet.

taxation-theft.rationale: Redistribution via tax is regarded as justice, not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents accept moral legislation (Prohibition) and liberty both.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Emphasis on solidarity, community and common good over individualism, though persons are of infinite worth.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from pacifist strands such as conscientious objectors.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democratic participation and solidarity matter far more than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Rejects acquisitive society values in public affairs and treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Tawney defined freedom as governance by good purposes and Rauschenbusch's reform seeks material means for all, so freedom needs material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; critique of power targets wealth and capital.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equal worth of all persons contradicts hereditarian racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Guild and Catholic strands favour functional representation but mainstream accepts party politics; split.

total-state.rationale: Democratic and freedom-valuing, with Christian pluralist and anarchist strands rejecting state control of all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a theme; prophetic rhetoric is of social, not national, renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Opposed to war and imperial domination.

bound-labor.rationale: Opposition to dependent labour and the bondage of the poor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; split between liberation theologians and others.

universal-morality.rationale: Christian ethics are claimed as universal truths, though not necessarily knowable by reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: Rauschenbusch holds the Kingdom of God as the supreme social good in which other goods are contained.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold divergent views.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source links Christian socialism to diaspora return rights; welcome for the stranger and national loyalties point different ways, so neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not a concern of the sources, apart from Welsh-language activism in Plaid Cymru, so adherents are left neutral on reviving a lost language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rauschenbusch's cooperation and democratic ideals, plus Ludlow's cooperatives, imply democratic voice for workers.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from preference for public provision and equality; Catholic strands support church schools funding.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from welfare and employment concerns.

economic-freedom.rationale: Tawney and others see unfettered economic freedom as rooted in greed and not a precondition of liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; moral example matters but laws are also sought.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred, supported by Plaid Cymru and Celtic Christian socialists; not a core tenet.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Faith is foundational to the position.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Concern for migrants and the stranger leads adherents to oppose restricting welfare to citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Care for the destitute is unconditional in tradition, though Ruskin proposed work for the unemployed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rauschenbusch stresses solidarity over predatory profit and Maurice sought Christian cooperation, but this competes with criticism of employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural destruction is contrary to the tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: The tradition is internationalist rather than geopolitical; liberation theology sympathises with dominated peoples but there is no stated common-front doctrine, so neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Solidarity is universal rather than national.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social Gospel linked to women's suffrage; stand inferred, with conservative strands dissenting.

ban-interest.rationale: Medieval Christian usury condemnation exists, but modern Christian socialists do not demand a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal worth and the civil-rights lineage of the Social Gospel oppose segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Mainstream views the state as reformable by democratic means, unlike Marxist theory.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from modern creation-care and justice emphases.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Hospitality for the stranger suggests against forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims conflict with the ethic of welcoming migrants.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from democratic ideals and support by left parties; not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Opposed to imperial attitudes; universal rather than national mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from Social Gospel's links to women's suffrage; not stated in sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Prophetic critique of the rich and powerful exists but the claim about political elites is not a distinctive tenet.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Human worth is infinite in this view, rejecting eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from justice emphasis and liberation-theology experience.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Active state for welfare and justice is central; contrary to the minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Tawney holds that every human being is of infinite importance, grounded in the Christian conception of persons.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Never addressed; equal treatment of persons favours uniform law, while religious-pluralist instincts favour community law, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from concerns of freedom of conscience; not addressed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Split between secularist and church school traditions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist-Leninist idea alien to the tradition.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democratic commitment and belief in common people's capacity.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist goal contrary to cooperative internationalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Violates the equal worth of persons and care for the stranger.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Christian pacifists say yes while most adherents accept state coercion for taxation and law.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rejects struggle as the engine and favours fellowship; criticises competition as unfraternal in tendency.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Commitment to democracy pulls against banning parties, while concern for human dignity pulls toward it; the sources are silent, so neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Tawney's view of freedom as governed by good purposes and concern for dependence on the powerful suggests agreement; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Christian socialists work democratically through persuasion and trust the common person.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Preferential concern for the poor is rooted in Isaiah, Matthew 25 and Luke 6 and appears throughout Rauschenbusch and liberation theology.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Support for unions and labour rights.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty traced to greed and institutions, not to population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Equal brotherhood and welcoming the stranger.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from standard democratic commitments.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from rights and democratic values.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Condemnation of profiteering by Basil and Chrysostom suggests approval of price controls in scarcity.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian and anti-wealth leanings; not discussed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Labour-affiliated Christian socialists accept party loyalty, but Christian conscience and anarchist strands resist binding votes; no stated position, so neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: The tradition seeks democratic socialism, not theocracy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Pacifist strands accept this, others support national defence; conscientious objectors were among Christian socialists.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred; some moralist Social Gospel reformers favoured censorship.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rauschenbusch wants property spread widely, but no source proposes banning rented housing; adherents reject such a prohibition as unnecessary.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred from pacifist and conscientious-objector strands, which oppose arming the citizenry as much as a professional army; sources do not address it directly.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rauschenbusch writes on rural cooperation but no moral claim of rural superiority.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources give no position on reunifying divided nations; peace and self-determination considerations conflict, so neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; anti-elitism directed at wealth.

death-penalty.rationale: Christian ethic of forgiveness and the pacifist tradition oppose execution.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Social Gospel was modernist and accepted science; Rauschenbusch combined social science with Christianity.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; moralist and liberal strands.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the care for strangers.

minority-language-support.rationale: Plaid Cymru Christian socialism and concern for minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; conscientious objection by Christian socialists suggests sympathy for exemptions, but equality before law pulls against, so neutral.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; communal solidarity favours conformity to fellowship while spiritual freedom of conscience favours eccentricity, so neutral.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from biblical jubilee and anti-usury themes and liberation theology.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Plaid Cymru and anticolonial socialism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Democratic commitment suggests sympathy for elected constitution-making, but no source addresses it and adherents work within existing parliaments, so neutral.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Universal brotherhood and priority to the poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Pacifist and Labour-linked tradition opposes nuclear arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Never addressed; democratic ideals favour direct election, but many adherents live under constitutional monarchies or parliamentary systems, so neutral.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rauschenbusch accepts private property insofar as it serves the common good and opposes neither public property nor social ownership.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Christian socialists want economic institutions to serve the common good and would not leave monetary policy beyond democratic direction, but the issue is not addressed in the sources; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The mainstream strand is pacifist-leaning and favours peacemaking, so ceding land for peace is acceptable; the sources do not address territorial claims, so inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Christian socialists reject Soviet communism, but their sources do not settle whether to call it state capitalism; adherents differ.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Stewardship of creation is a recurring Christian theme and fits the social concern of the tradition; inferred, not a defining text.

collective-defense.rationale: Pacifist and Labour-affiliated strands disagree about military alliances, so adherents are split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Justice for the oppressed and the prophetic tradition lead adherents to reject conquest without consent; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Social Gospel wants the churches to engage society and challenge power, not be controlled by the state; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The reforming strand worked within parliamentary Britain and the American republic, where constitutional monarchy or ceremonial presidency is accepted; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Pacifist strands and the emphasis on peace make adherents wary of force to hold a region, though not unanimously; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Cooperative and decentralised arrangements fit its communal ethos; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The tradition stresses the equality of all before God and opposes idolatry of rulers; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Redistribution and priority for the poor point to progressive taxation; inferred from its welfare-state aims.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Social Gospel treats sin and poverty as largely social and structural, so changing conditions changes people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rulers answer to a higher justice and to the community; inferred from the Gospel emphasis on justice.

space-expansion.rationale: The tradition does not address it, and nothing in its principles points either way.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Its democratic, egalitarian outlook favours rule by the many; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Glorifying leaders is idolatry in Christian terms, so adherents oppose a leader cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Adherents are divided on family and social questions, as the summary notes.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Christian socialism seeks reform by democratic persuasion rather than class war.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Acts picture of shared goods and concern for the poor support wider land access; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The Gospel's concern for the stranger and the dispossessed supports return; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Solidarity and the equal worth of all peoples oppose nationalist territorial claims; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Democratic, persuasion-based politics opposes legal punishment of belief; inferred, though some adherents are traditional.

women-must-cover.rationale: Social Gospel reformers backed women's equality, though adherents are split on social questions; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, so split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Gospel universalism opposes ethnic unity projects; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Social Gospel reformers pressed for equal treatment including on race; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Tawney and the movement hold that faith and moral insight shape economic order, not only material change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Social Gospel reformers opposed trusts and concentrated economic power; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Wealth held as a trust for the common good suggests firms should answer for failure, not be rescued; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Democratic reformers value institutions, constitutional protections and the poor's equal standing; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Social Gospel supported equality for women, but quotas are not addressed and adherents split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Solidarity and cooperation across peoples oppose closed autarky; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Social Gospel pressed for child-labour and union protections; inferred for binding trade standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Social Principles of Jesus stress service, cooperation and solidarity over profit as the motive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Christian socialism favours pacifism and democratic persuasion over armed action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Tawney's equal worth of persons opposes inherited privilege; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Indifferent: Christian socialists do not address history curricula, and adherents are split between national and universal framings.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the universal brotherhood and solidarity in Rauschenbusch and Tawney; some early British Christian Socialists were imperial paternalists, so it is contested.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the universalist, often pacifist, emphasis of the strand, which puts the Kingdom of God above national loyalty; not directly addressed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Adherents are divided on social questions; Social Gospel racial egalitarianism supports colour-blind rules while solidarity with the disadvantaged supports remedial measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the strand's hostility to usury and finance and its call for common ownership of the economy; not a stated programme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Christian socialists seek change by democratic persuasion and reform rather than waiting for a collapse; inferred from their reformist strategy.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the strand's universalism and peace emphasis; not addressed in its sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: Mainstream Christian socialists favour reform and fair dealing within and between nations rather than withdrawal; liberation theologians would differ.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Rauschenbusch and Tawney stress solidarity and the equal worth of all workers rather than a privileged section; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Equal worth of persons is central to Tawney and Rauschenbusch, and the Social Gospel took positions on race and gender equality, so owners' licence to discriminate is rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from Christian respect for human dignity and the movement's democratic reformism; not directly addressed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the Gospel's universal brotherhood and the Social Gospel's concern for justice to the weak; no source addresses colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Christian socialists are democrats, but the British strand of Maurice and Kingsley worked within a constitutional monarchy; inferred as split.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the reforming, democratic-persuasion method, which accepts majority decisions within a framework of conscience and rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the prophetic Christian tradition of judging rulers who oppress the poor; contested by quietist Christians.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The movement sought change through democratic and parliamentary reform, as in its Labour affiliation; inferred for the monarch-versus-parliament question.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from Christian ethics of compassion for creation; the sources do not discuss animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from mainstream Christian acceptance of animal use with a duty of kindness; not addressed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Its core is the Gospel duty of the better-off to the poor, though Christian socialists seek structural change rather than paternal charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Social Gospel and Christian socialists hold that faith must be lived out in social and political reform, rejecting retreat from public affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Tawney-style critiques of commercial culture exist, but the Marxist theory of media pacification is not central; inferred as split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian hegemony account is not part of the tradition; adherents stress moral persuasion and are split on the point.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Liberation theology adopts dependency analysis, but the mainstream reforming strand is less explicit; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the universal brotherhood of the Gospel, which rejects birth-based civic privilege.

party-own-road.rationale: The movement has no international party line; inferred that national self-determination of reform parties is accepted.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the duty of the rich toward the poor, applied internationally; not directly addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from the pacifist and peace-seeking strands and rejection of war for national claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the Gospel's equality of persons, which opposes descent-based rule, though it supports redress.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from Christian socialists' opposition to fascism and commitment to democracy; not documented in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic, non-Marxist, anti-statist-coercion stance; contested by liberation-theology strands.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The Social Gospel descends from the Christian abolitionist tradition; inferred that slavery is seen as the central cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from concern for the victims of past injustice; adherents may differ.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from concern for all in need; not addressed by the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Adherents care about all victims but are divided on equal-seriousness framing; inferred as split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the Gospel's universalism; liberation theology also favours local forms, so adherents vary.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its pacifist strand and democratic, civilian-led reform method.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from concern for the dignity of labour and for the family and the poor; not directly documented.

filial-duty.rationale: Honouring parents is a biblical commandment and family solidarity fits the movement, though it is not a defining issue; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Reformers favoured democratic persuasion and universal participation over rule by a selected elite; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is split between anti-capitalist concern about foreign capital and internationalist solidarity. Inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Adherents are split along church lines on divorce, from Catholic opposition to liberal Labour-affiliated reformers.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Democratic, communal and cooperative ideals favour accountable representatives; inferred from Rauschenbusch on democracy.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Solidarity and the welfare state are central, so pensions through private savings accounts run against the movement's cooperative economics.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rauschenbusch treats property as a trust for humanity and the movement accepts social ownership, which supports land held for use; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Democratic reformers want elected legislatures to control public money; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Concern for the poor and migrants and minorities suggests tolerance for linguistic diversity; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Universal fellowship and care for the stranger run against excluding foreigners from owning land; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The Social Gospel campaigned on race and justice, so judging policy by outcomes is plausible, but this is inferred and views vary.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Tawney and Rauschenbusch condemn greed and the acquisitive society, and the movement cites Gospel warnings about wealth.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Pacifist and peace-minded strands and Rauschenbusch on war make arming insurgents unlikely to be supported; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Christian socialists stress peace and self-determination, so force to hold allies in a bloc is rejected; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Tawney's acquisitive society and Rauschenbusch's critique of profit-driven power treat mammon's hold on public life as a central evil.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are inferred to be split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; family-supporting values pull toward it, while universal solidarity pulls against nationalist framing.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; hospitality to the stranger suggests opposing exclusion by residence, though stewardship of the commons pulls the other way.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed directly; the right to work and a just livelihood are Social Gospel themes, so a job guarantee is inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Social Gospel's optimism about reform leaned toward this but the claim is not addressed; split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Biblical teaching to respect authority (Romans 13) and a reformist, parliamentary outlook point toward a general duty to obey, though conscience can override.

non-intervention.rationale: Pacifist strands oppose intervention while others accept humanitarian action; split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Christian socialists backed unions generally, including industrial unions in the Social Gospel era; the form was not a defining question.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Universal brotherhood and the biblical condemnation of false witness stand against scapegoating a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Mainstream adherents hold marriage as a sacred institution to be protected, though the Social Gospel was concerned with other issues; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic accountability and Tawney's concern for equal citizenship.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; cooperative and distributist strands favour local economies but mainstream adherents are split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Christian socialists work through churches, parties and unions, which are formal bodies.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Universalist solidarity favours international cooperation over national supremacy; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Christianity inspires the movement but adherents favour inclusive, democratic and pluralist community over a religiously defined nation; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Christian socialism stresses the equal worth of persons and peoples and the Kingdom of God over hierarchy; I infer a preference for equal dealings between states, not ritual tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from its principle of solidarity and sharing according to need (Acts 4), which favours pooling resources across regions over regional retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from Rauschenbusch's view of property as a trust for the common good, which leaves personal goods private while social ownership extends to productive wealth.

defeat-communism.rationale: The movement is largely pacifist and reformist and rejects class war; I infer it favours peaceful coexistence and persuasion over a campaign to defeat communism, though it opposes Marxist atheism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Adherents back publicly funded welfare provision and cooperatives but the sources say nothing on who should deliver services, so I treat it as split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Christian socialists hold that faith answers lasting human needs and is the source of their politics; the claim that religion is a consoling illusion that fades is the Marxist view they reject.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Rauschenbusch and Tawney condemn the competitive, acquisitive system as contrary to the Gospel, so adherents see it as mainly harmful; I infer they would not credit it as a foundation for a better order.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Social Gospel campaigned for women's rights and labour reform, but adherents are split on gender questions and I found no stated view tying equality to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditional-family emphasis and church-line splits on social questions; it backs welfare support for families more than public replacement of domestic work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred from its concern for ordinary people and the view that language policy by compulsion is an illiberal state overreach.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from its ethic of keeping promises and justice for the weak, consistent with its answers on indigenous authority and colonial treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Acts 4 sharing of goods is cited as a model, and Christian communitarian strands favour cooperative communities, though the mainstream reformers sought national reform instead.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the equal worth of all peoples in the Gospel; a state policy of settling the majority in minority regions to bind them conflicts with justice for minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Christian socialists reject both competitive capitalism and Marxist class war and propose a cooperative third course, though some adherents back state socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: its universalist reading of the Gospel gives little weight to one people's historical or religious claim over residents now living there.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred from its Christian ethics of justice and neighbourly love; no strand denies the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: its reform strands focus on economic justice and generally do not support criminalising adult private conduct, though some adherents hold traditional views.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Christian socialists pursue change through democratic persuasion and reform, and oppose suppressing opponents.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the Social Gospel and Labour-affiliated strands favour a free civil order, not state punishment of belief.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from its Gospel concern for the poor and its social ethics, which condemn exploiting subject peoples.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the statement is Islamic doctrine; Christian socialists include pacifist strands and don't hold it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream reforming strand works by democratic means and does not endorse forcibly removing rulers over religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from its cooperative, democratic ideals; Christian socialists favour cooperatives and strong unions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its concern for the poor and its Social Gospel analysis of structural injustice.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Adherents are divided on moral and social questions, so no majority position is documented.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred: many Christian adherents oppose assisted dying on sanctity-of-life grounds, though some support it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: Christian socialism sees itself as a left project joining Christian ethics to the labour movement.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: its critique of competitive acquisitiveness and its call for cooperative work extend naturally to alienated labour, though it uses moral rather than Marxist language.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: its ethic of neighbourly love and Christian universalism, though some adherents share concerns about Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Adherents are split: many believe authority is ultimately from God, but the democratic reform strands also stress popular consent.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: its reform strands would tolerate religious dress, and many oppose a ban on religious expression in public life.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its concern for workers' protection and justice; not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: its mainstream seeks cooperatives, unions and a welfare state alongside markets, though it also wants social ownership.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Adherents are split: pacifist and anarchist Christians would abolish armies, while the Labour-affiliated mainstream accepts defence.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: its Gospel concern for the poor and shared-goods ideal reject letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Foreign policy is outside its defining concerns and adherents are split, with pacifist strands favouring neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Christian socialists favoured democratic, fraternal institutions and the Social Gospel's equality of persons; inherited office is inferred to be rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The movement's cooperative tradition (Ludlow, Maurice) and Christian distrust of usury suggest support for cost-based user-owned credit; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Priority to the poor leads Christian socialists, e.g. in debt-relief campaigns, to oppose austerity; inferred, since the sources do not cover the IMF.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal worth of every person and the movement's drive to give workers a political voice make wealth-based voting unacceptable.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Stewardship of creation and women's equality appear in modern Christian left thinking, but linking them as one logic of domination is not a shared doctrine; adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Tawney's critique of the acquisitive society and the Social Gospel's attack on treating people as commodities resemble this claim, though not in Marxist terms; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Social Gospel and Tawney criticised wealth's power over public life; inferred that adherents see formal freedoms as hollow under inequality.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Reformist, parliamentary methods and the biblical emphasis on justice favour rule by public law; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Brotherhood of all people under God is central to the movement, and the Labour-affiliated body opposes racial discrimination.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources give no basis, and adherents are likely split on direct online decision-making.

open-government-data.rationale: Reforming democratic outlook favours accountable government; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The reforming strand works within liberal democracies and has not sought legal limits on marriage; inferred from its mainstream scope.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Shunning a religious minority contradicts the neighbourly love at the movement's core; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed by the tradition, but the Social Gospel and Christians on the Left stress democracy and the dignity and equal worth of ordinary people; deliberation by citizens chosen by lot is a modest inference from that and is contested.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The reforming Social Gospel strand reread Scripture and doctrine for industrial conditions rather than holding to inherited rulings, though traditionalist Christian socialists would disagree; inferred from the movement's reforming approach.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Christian socialists condemn greed and the accumulation of wealth as against the Gospel and favour cooperative and social ownership, seeing concentrated wealth as a threat to community and fairness.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Adherents are divided on same-sex relations, as the profile notes for same-sex marriage; the Labour-affiliated mainstream is liberal on it but others are traditional.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Christian socialism is rooted in Christian faith and sees the Gospel as its basis, so promoting atheism through schools is contrary to its core.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream reforming strand works through democratic institutions and accepts the state's role in order, though pacifist and anarchist Christians would answer differently.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents have no shared position on consociational power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Christian socialists hold that charity alone is insufficient and that justice requires structural reform and a welfare state, as Tawney and the Social Gospel argued.

term-limits.rationale: The tradition does not address term limits; adherents are indifferent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; its emphasis on community and democratic reform is compatible with but does not require delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from the Christian ethic of stewardship and care for humanity, though the tradition did not address extinction risk directly.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split: the Anglican and Protestant Social Gospel strands support women's ordination, while Catholic and some other strands do not.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the Social Gospel and Labour-affiliated mainstream favour equality of the sexes, but traditional Christian socialists may keep a headship view.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Gospel's concern for the stranger and the Social Gospel's universalism.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its welfare-state and anti-exploitation commitments applied to housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from social ownership to reform, so no clear position is inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its pacifist and anti-militarist strands and the Social Gospel's emphasis on cooperation over national service.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from its strong pacifist and peace-movement strand.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; pacifists would agree but Labour-affiliated reformers often supported alliances, so adherents are inferred as split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its moral concern for the oppressed and for justice.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Tawney's critique of the acquisitive society attacks property and income that serve no function, and Rauschenbusch condemns profit from ownership rather than labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Christian pacifists and anarchists hold this, while the mainstream reforming strand accepts just-war reasoning, so adherents are split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its universalist Christian ethic, which does not ground identity in ancient national origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; many Christian adherents hold more traditional views of sex, so this is inferred as mildly negative.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are divided on social and moral questions.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Christian martyrdom is honoured, but honouring those who die for the nation as saints sits poorly with its universalism, so this is inferred as mildly negative.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Social Gospel frames social reform as the struggle to build the kingdom of God against an evil social order, though it is not a good-versus-evil politics in the literal sense.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; no position is documented.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents combine moral renewal with state reform.

god-not-male.rationale: Adherents are divided between progressive and traditional Christian views on this.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Adherents are divided between liberationist and traditional approaches to scripture.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from its universalist ethic of brotherhood and cooperation, which opposes ethnic economic ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its universalism, which does not support ethnic territorial consolidation.

independent-unions.rationale: Christian socialists back strong, member-run unions as part of a cooperative economic order, as in Tawney and the Labour-affiliated movement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Christian socialism works through democratic reform and wants economic power answerable to the people; inferred from its democratic persuasion approach.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Christian socialists favour social ownership and a welfare state, so basic local services staying public fits their programme.

second-chamber.rationale: Not discussed in its sources and British, American and other adherents differ on institutions.

municipal-property.rationale: Its models are cooperatives and public ownership at several levels, not municipal ownership alone; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not committed either way on confederal structures.

family-wage.rationale: Social Gospel and Christian socialist calls for a living wage to support households fit this, though the question is not directly sourced.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not discussed; a caution-favouring, protective regulatory stance is inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed; concern for the sick pulls one way, scepticism of technological promises the other.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from preference for public accountability over untraceable private finance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; adherents are likely split between privacy and accountability.

person-over-state.rationale: Christian ethics holds the dignity of each person before God, which is why the Social Gospel judges institutions by how they treat persons.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Christian socialism is grounded in the Gospel and treats human life as spiritual as well as material, so politics should serve both.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not discussed; a mainstream reformist inclination to keep parliament sovereign is inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not discussed; adherents likely split between stewardship concerns and concern for the poor.

dense-cities.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from its social-reform urban roots and stewardship of creation.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Its Gospel-based universal brotherhood treats all people as equal before God, so organising politics by race is rejected.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from universalist Christian equality; not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Many adherents are pacifist or just-war thinkers, and the mainstream is reluctant about aggressive war; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Christian socialists stress universal fellowship over nationality, but did not address language and nation directly; adherents split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the Social Gospel's universalism and democratic reformism, which favour common citizenship over separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred from its internationalist, pacifist-leaning outlook.

free-public-college.rationale: Tawney campaigned for universal public education and the Workers' Educational Association, and the welfare-state agenda of the movement extends to free access.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed historically; modern groups stress stewardship of creation, but there is no stated preference for taxes over regulation.

future-generations.rationale: Stewardship of God's creation and of property held in trust for the common good (s2 notes property as a stewardship) imply a duty to later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Adherents are split: some stress care and peace as Christian virtues, while others resist gender essentialism; inferred, not stated.

arms-reduction.rationale: Christian socialists draw on the Sermon on the Mount and peacemaking, and pacifism has been prominent among them; reduction of arms follows.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the moral demand for honesty and peace-making; secret treaties conflict with it, but sources do not discuss it.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; adherents support regulating capital in the public interest but have no stated view on border controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed; the reforming strand works through the democratic state, though pacifist and anarchist Christians dissent. Inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pacifist currents and Christians on the Left oppose war, and the Social Gospel tradition urged conscientious objection, though not all adherents agree.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Christian socialists from Maurice and Ludlow to Tawney backed trade unions and cooperation, and the Labour-affiliated movement backs unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Support for low-paid workers fits their welfare-state aims; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not discussed; priority to the poor and public spending suggests opposition to binding limits. Inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Concern for the poor extends to global justice campaigning, though the sources focus on domestic reform; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement pursues democratic persuasion and reform, not class war or overthrow of the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Cooperation is favoured, but Christian socialists generally have a view of the economy to build; inferred as split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Stewardship of creation is a theme, but pricing nature as capital is not a Christian-socialist idea; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not addressed; universal Christian brotherhood sits uneasily with sacralising the nation. Inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Mercy for debtors and concern for the poor suggest support; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Human dignity grounded in being made in God's image is central to their ethics, so a given human nature is affirmed.

public-service-media.rationale: Support for public provision suggests sympathy for independent public media; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Most Christian socialists hold Christianity's claims as distinctive, though many are ecumenical; inferred, as the question is outside their social programme.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Social Gospel and British Christian socialists backed cooperative credit and protection of the vulnerable from moneylenders; inferred from their concern for the poor.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Pacifist and Labour-affiliated strands, including support for nuclear disarmament campaigns, make unilateral keeping unpopular; inferred, low confidence.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Christian Socialist Movement is affiliated with the Labour Party as the party of working people; inferred from that link.

ban-fgm.rationale: Protection of the vulnerable and the dignity of women favours a ban, though adherents differ on custom and law; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal treatment of women as children of God favours equal property rights; inferred, as the tradition is mostly silent on land law.

one-language-many-names.rationale: No stated view on language classification; neutral inference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Christian socialists prefer public regulation for the common good over leaving harms to private litigation; inferred from their reform tradition.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Adherents are split between secular elected lawmaking and respect for established church and traditional roles; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Stewardship of creation leads many adherents to put the environment ahead of unrestricted liberty; inferred, adherents vary.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Emphasis on reform and mercy favours judicial discretion over fixed sentences; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Hospitality to strangers is stressed but adherents differ on state requirements; neutral inference.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the movement's strong support for unions and collective bargaining, which suggests acceptance of shared union obligations.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on the equal worth of all and on democratic inclusion of the poor.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its reforming, pluralist tradition, though some strands favour established churches.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Christian socialists treating democracy as a means to fellowship and a cooperative order, not a mere method.

premarital-sex.rationale: Adherents are divided on sexual morality, from traditional Christian teaching to liberal views.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the stress on the dignity and voice of ordinary people, which makes shutdowns hard to justify.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: it backs a welfare state but has no stated position on how benefits should be delivered.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from Tawney's equal worth of persons and the Social Gospel's reform agenda.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its view of the Gospel as liberating; adherents would reject religion as a main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its Gospel-based equal worth of all people.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: No stated view; adherents back equality but the issue is not discussed in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the view that wealth is held for the common good rather than as absolute possession; no stated position on first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the Social Gospel and Labour-aligned emphasis on justice and peace; not discussed directly.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Social Gospel mainstream read Scripture ethically rather than literally, though adherents vary, so this is inferred and contested.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the movement's concern for justice for the marginalised; not addressed directly.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The mainstream reforming strand pursued democratic persuasion and cooperation, not state planning defended against all comers; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the strand's reliance on democratic reform and Labour politics; indirect election is not discussed.

national-church-status.rationale: Adherents are split: Anglican socialists accepted an established church, while Nonconformists and others opposed privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from concern for the marginalised and for local self-determination; not addressed directly.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from democratic commitments and the principle that people affected should decide; not addressed directly.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view on colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the Gospel's warnings against greed and its picture of shared goods; the strand stresses simplicity but not self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from protecting Indigenous peoples to universalist openness.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from pacifists opposed to conscription of anyone to those favouring equal duties.

missingStatements.text: Wealth should be treated as a trust held for the common good rather than as the owner's absolute possession.
missingStatements.rationale: Rauschenbusch describes property as a stewardship held from God and for humanity, central to the Christian-socialist critique of acquisition.

missingStatements.text: The material wealth of society should be shared according to the example of the early Christian community.
missingStatements.rationale: Acts 4 sharing of goods is cited as an early model of communal economics.

missingStatements.text: Private property is justified only so far as it serves the common good.
missingStatements.rationale: Rauschenbusch accepts private property insofar as it serves the common good and opposes neither public property nor social ownership.

notes: Strands differ: liberation theology and Christians for Socialism accept class struggle and revolution, Christian anarchists reject the state and violence, and the Catholic hierarchy (Pius XI) called Christian socialism contradictory. Social-issue answers split along church lines.
